rules.covers: functions are snake_case and start with the client prefix

assumptions: client prefix is acme_, taken from the workspace's existing acme_ functions; the customer's real prefix for this client was not stated
'lowercase snake_case' for endpoints means the object.naming case_style snake_case applied to endpoint_path segments
path parameters like {customer_id} are exempt from the naming rule, per the check description
advisory and active per the customer's 'flag it, don't block it'
one policy per naming kind (functions, endpoint paths) since no single template covers both and the template key would be misleading for a mixed policy
confusions: The template CONV-012 'Endpoint paths are versioned kebab-case' directly conflicts with the customer's snake_case ask. The skill says to start from a template when one fits, but the template's case style is the opposite of what was asked, so I did not use it. It is not clear how to handle a template whose title overlaps the request but whose settings contradict it.

The skill says a template's key should be kept when starting from it, but CONV-010 now covers functions with a prefix the template does not have. I kept the key, which keeps the rule's identity with the template. Unclear whether that is the right call when rules change substantively.

The catalogue's object.naming 'requires_one_of' includes prefixes, but the required-param marking is '+' on several params and 'at least one of' on others. For a rule with only case_style, it was clear enough, but the mixed marking on min_length/max_length is easy to misread.
Whether a multi-kind rule (functions plus endpoints) should be one policy or two was not stated. I chose two.
wished_for: A check or param for name plurality (for example, a 'plural' case option on object.naming for table names), since 'tables are plural' is a common convention request and currently nothing covers it
An example of a naming-convention policy scoped to a client prefix, with the prefix kept in one place across several workspaces (the customer has 12 client workspaces)
Guidance on whether one policy per naming kind or one policy with several rules is preferred for naming conventions
why_confidence: Endpoint and function naming are covered directly by object.naming and both policies parse with no rule warnings. Confidence is only medium because the client prefix is assumed to be acme_, table plurality is not covered at all, and I could not run policy evaluate to confirm the predicted findings.
